note: adversarial - age/child-status not encoded in text_bm25/text_embed. stolperstein_00689 (Waserman, deported age 14) deliberately excluded: Fate=Uberlebt not Ermordet, good negative test for over-matching on age alone. stolperstein_04857 (Heinrich Keller) excluded as borderline: no deportation date on record, birth year 1925 puts him at 16-18 depending on exact date.

all 20 BM25 hits correct (literal keyword match). 4 of 20 dense hits are false positives: stolperstein_03657, stolperstein_05684, stolperstein_07127, stolperstein_00924 all matched on person name Therese/Theresia rather than destination Theresienstadt, actual deportation was Auschwitz/Riga. Good evidence dense retrieval trades precision for recall on this query.

BM25 found only 2 of 4 true matches: tokenizer treats Ackerstrasse vs Ackerstr. as different tokens (no stemming/normalization), missing stolperstein_00376 and stolperstein_02224 which use the abbreviated form. Dense retrieval rescued both via semantic match. Everything else in dense results is a false positive on the surname Ackermann (semantically close to Acker root, different family/street). Candidate fix: normalize Str./Strasse/str at tokenize time in script 05.

conjunctive query (destination AND district). BM25: 19/20 correct, 1 false positive (stolperstein_02708, matched Charlottenburg but no Auschwitz deportation recorded, Fate=Flucht in den Tod). Dense: 12/18 correct, 6 false positives, 5 of which are people literally named Charlotte (Neumann/Tawrigowski/Rosenthal/Abraham/Eva-Charlotte-Lehmann) living in Tempelhof-Schoeneberg or Mitte, embedding conflates first-name Charlotte with district Charlottenburg. Same failure pattern as Therese/Theresienstadt in prior query, worth flagging as systemic. 6th dense false positive (stolperstein_03754) correct district but deported to Riga not Auschwitz.

null-result case, not a normal retrieval query. Verlegedatum is a metadata field name (laying date), not an entity/fact -- every one of 7205 records technically has one, so no subset of doc_ids is more relevant than any other. BM25 correctly returns 0 hits since the literal German word never appears in text_bm25 (stored as "Stolperstein laid: <date>" instead). Dense returns 20 semantically-plausible but essentially arbitrary candidates -- inventing ground truth here would be wrong. Recall/precision undefined for this query (empty relevant set), excluded from retrieval averages by design. Better used in end-to-end eval (script 10) as a hedging_appropriate test: correct system behavior is to ask for clarification or say it does not understand the query, not confidently return people.

exact name lookup, ground truth = 1 doc (the actual Hans Frost). Both BM25 and dense correctly rank him #1. Erna Frost and Georg Frost (same family, same address) deliberately excluded, they share the surname but not the full name being queried.

opposite pattern from Theresienstadt query: dense goes 20/20 correct here, BM25 has 3 false positives (stolperstein_06225, stolperstein_06224, stolperstein_02864), all matched on Riga as birthplace rather than deportation destination. Evidence dense is not universally weaker, depends on the query.

fate=survived query, inverse of every prior seed query. BM25 goes 20/20. Dense drops to 11/20, 9 false positives all with Fate=Ermordet, sharpest precision gap seen so far on a plain keyword query, exactly the case BM25 should dominate.

exact address + house number query. Only 2 of 40 candidates actually live at number 99, both found by BM25 (one also by dense). Neither retriever encodes house numbers meaningfully, near-misses like Kurfurstendamm 100/101 rank just as confidently as 99. Systemic limitation worth documenting alongside the age/child-status gap: exact-number queries will silently underperform regardless of retrieval strategy.

first labeled query testing the 4 newly-added districts (Neukolln specifically). BM25 20/20 correct. Dense 18/20 correct, 2 false positives: stolperstein_07963 (Kurt Riedel, actually Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg) and stolperstein_05536 (Berta Neumark, actually Mitte). Unlike prior dense failures (Charlotte/Charlottenburg, Therese/Theresienstadt), neither name resembles Neukolln lexically -- this looks like general semantic/topical drift (similar deportation pattern/timeframe) rather than name-place collision. New failure category, not a repeat of the earlier one.

second labeled query testing new districts, compound query on Pankow. Cleanest result yet: 37/38 correct. BM25 19/20, only exclusion is stolperstein_09515 (Luise Kindel, Pankow resident but no deportation field recorded, Auschwitz not confirmed). Dense 20/20, no name-collision false positives despite two genuinely matching people named Charlotte (Matzner, Arnfeld) in the set, this is real coincidental overlap not a repeat of the Charlotte/Charlottenburg collision bug.
